episodes.summary: Birth and description of the family home in Thrissur, Kerala, built by grandfather.
Description of the house's roof and monsoon rain.
Description of the open courtyard with a tulsi plant and mother's daily ritual.
Father's profession as a schoolmaster and his evening routine on the verandah.
Description of the narrator's siblings and their shared living space.
Description of the kitchen, hearth, and brass vessels.
Grandmother grinding rice batter on a heavy stone.
Narrator's childhood curiosity about how the house worked.
Description of the roof beams and their durability.
Description of the well and mango tree behind the kitchen.
Description of the neighbors: a carpenter and a widow with hens.
Description of the lane and the walk to school.
Father reading aloud to the family on the verandah in the evenings.
Arrival of electricity in the lane and the first bulb in the courtyard.
Description of the family's simple diet and cooking methods.
Festival days with rice flour patterns and visiting relatives.
Narrator's sensory memories of the house and its influence on his life.
Introduction of childhood friend Gopalan (Gopi) who lived nearby and repaired bicycles with his father.
Spending afternoons in Gopi's shed learning about bicycle mechanics.
Building a water wheel in the stream behind the paddy fields during the summer the narrator turned eleven.
Gopi's struggles in school and the narrator helping him with arithmetic using pebbles on the verandah.
Gopi leaving school at thirteen to work full-time with his father, and the narrator missing him in class.
Gopi gifting the narrator a brass bell for his bicycle when he left for engineering college.
time_references: When I went away to the engineering college

episodes.summary: Gopi expanding his father's shed into a proper shop and the narrator visiting him in Kerala.
Gopi and the narrator reminiscing about the water wheel in the stream.
Gopi's death and the narrator receiving a photograph of the shop with the old bench.
Reflection on the enduring nature of the friendship with Gopi, built on tools and repairs.

repetitions.rationale: Both episodes describe the same event of building and reminiscing about the water wheel in the stream.
quoted_passages: We talked about the wheel in the stream more than anything else.
He once told me that he still looked at running water and thought of our paddles.

episodes.summary: Meeting Mister Duncan Hale, a Scotsman and chief engineer, in Abu Dhabi in 1983.
Hale's silent tour of the plant and his lesson about observing the operators, not just the machines.
Hale making the narrator sit with operators for a week to listen and learn from them.
Hale teaching the narrator to keep an honest logbook, including mistakes, and the narrator's first recorded error.
Evening gatherings at Hale's flat for tea, shortbread, and discussions, including his love for technical books and bagpipes.
Hale's habit of naming pumps and valves after Scottish rivers, which the operators adopted.
Hale's appreciation for Carnatic music and the narrator bringing him a veena recital tape.
Hale working alongside the team during long nights and his leadership style of humility and collaboration.
Hale gifting the narrator a brass slide rule upon his promotion to supervisor.
Hale's retirement to a town near Aberdeen and his correspondence with the narrator for twenty years.
The narrator reflecting on Hale's mentorship and how it shaped his own approach to leading juniors.
Starting first job as a junior design engineer at a pump manufacturing works in Coimbatore in 1975.
Living in a rented room above a tea shop with a retired nurse landlady who served idli every morning.
Mister Raghavan, the owner, walking the shed every morning and knowing every worker by name.
Receiving a salary of 450 rupees a month and sending a quarter home, with mother asking about eating habits.
Enjoying the stillness of the compound on Sundays.
Walking past the lathe shop in the evenings and watching apprentices sweep up metal curls.
Learning from workers, especially Foreman Subramaniam, who taught the narrator how to listen to a bearing.
Building a test rig for pumps and taking pride in initials on every pump that left the works.
Dealing with a difficult customer from Palakkad who returned a pump three times due to a dropped well.
Playing weekly cricket matches on a dusty ground with a taped tennis ball and drinking tea afterward.
Reflecting on the lessons learned from the pump works, including patience and the dignity of machines.
Feeling restless after three years and deciding to apply for a job in the Gulf.
Expressing gratitude to the pump works for giving a footing and still listening to pumps humming in buildings.
The narrator describes his first flight from Kochi to Abu Dhabi in 1979 at age 27.
The narrator recalls the intense heat and humidity upon arriving in Abu Dhabi.
A company driver meets the narrator at the airport with a misspelled name card.
The narrator describes the drive to the city and his first impressions of Abu Dhabi.
The narrator moves into a shared house near the plant with four other bachelors.
The narrator describes the shared living arrangements and house rules.
The narrator learns to cook dal and chapati from a Punjabi engineer named Harbans.
The narrator describes the plant's purpose: turning seawater into drinking water.
The narrator writes letters home every Sunday and cherishes the replies.
The narrator describes how Abu Dhabi gradually felt like home due to the generosity of its people.
The narrator's wife, Lakshmi, joins him in Abu Dhabi after their arranged marriage.
The narrator's sons, Arun and Vivek, are born and grow up in Abu Dhabi.
The narrator reflects on his unplanned long-term stay in Abu Dhabi and his career at the plant.
The narrator reflects on having roots in both Kerala and Abu Dhabi.
The narrator takes an overnight train to Madras for an engineering college interview at age seventeen.
The narrator loses his shoes from the train and reflects on the incident.
The narrator borrows oversized sandals for the interview and faces amusement from the panel.
The narrator observes the scenery and vendors during the train journey.
The narrator witnesses the engine change at Palakkad and studies the coupling mechanism.
The narrator shares tamarind sweets with a girl and her mother on the train.
The narrator visits the beach in Madras after the interview and reflects on the ocean.
The narrator returns home and receives new shoes, with his family laughing about the sandals.
The narrator reflects on how the journey marked the beginning of his traveling life.
The narrator describes his wedding to Lakshmi in 1981 at a temple near Guruvayur.
The narrator recalls the story of losing his shoes on the Madras train and his cousins laughing about it during the wedding.
The narrator and Lakshmi celebrate their fortieth anniversary with a small dinner, and their sons ask for the wedding feast story.

repetitions.acknowledgement_quote: I believe I told you about my shoes and the Madras train last time.
repetitions.rationale: The narrator recounts the same event of losing his shoes on the Madras train, now referenced during his wedding.
quoted_passages: I had to leave my shoes outside,
my cousins, who knew the old story, laughed at me.

repetitions.rationale: The narrator retells the wedding feast story during the fortieth anniversary celebration.
quoted_passages: They asked for the old story of the wedding feast, and I told it again.

episodes.summary: The narrator describes his early morning routine, including tea and the drive to the plant.
time_references: before the sun was properly up

episodes.summary: The narrator describes the plant's structure and its purpose of desalinating seawater.
The narrator details his morning inspection routine at the plant, including checking gauges and writing in a notebook.
The narrator describes the working conditions in the plant, including heat, noise, and interactions with operators.
The narrator meets with the shift supervisor to discuss plant operations and potential issues.
The narrator reviews the maintenance list and plans work for the day, focusing on combating scale buildup.
The narrator attends a short morning meeting with managers.
The narrator describes his lunch routine, including eating Lakshmi's packed meal at his desk.
The narrator writes reports in the afternoon, emphasizing the importance of recommendations.
The narrator conducts a second round of inspections in the late afternoon, enjoying the golden light.
The narrator signs the logbook and hands over duties to the evening engineer before leaving.
The narrator describes his drive home and the changing colors of the sky.
The narrator describes his evening routine at home, including helping his sons with homework and family dinner.
The narrator plays chess with Arun and reads the newspaper after dinner.
The narrator reflects on the satisfaction of his daily routine and compares the plant to a living body.

repetitions.rationale: Both episodes describe the plant's purpose of turning seawater into fresh water.
quoted_passages: Its purpose was to boil seawater and capture the steam, which condensed into fresh water.

repetitions.rationale: Both episodes reflect on the narrator's long-term career at the plant in Abu Dhabi.
quoted_passages: I kept that uh routine for thirty-five years, and I would happily keep it again.

episodes.summary: Description of the school building and its surroundings, including the banyan tree.
Daily school routine, including prayers, multiplication tables, and writing on slates.
Love for mathematics, especially geometry, and the geometry teacher's advice.
English lessons from a worn reader and reading stories to sister Meena.
Science classes with a magnet and mercury, and father's role as a teacher.
Prize day in the courtyard and receiving the mathematics prize three times.
Monsoon challenges in the classroom and lunch under the banyan tree.
School discipline, including being caned once for laughing during an inspection.
Exams in a hall and the joy of seeing good results.
Reflection on the value of school discipline and the pleasure of learning.
The narrator and his team fix a critical pump vibration issue at the Abu Dhabi plant in 1998 by diagnosing a bearing fault and replacing it overnight.
The narrator reflects on the pride and reward of the pump repair, including the team's reaction and the lasting impact on young engineers.
The narrator expresses pride in his sons' careers and credits their success to their own efforts, with support from him and Lakshmi.
The narrator reflects on the pump repair as the finest moment of his working life, valuing careful listening, teamwork, and restoring the machine.

repetitions.rationale: Both episodes involve diagnosing a pump issue by listening to its bearing, a technique learned from Foreman Subramaniam in Coimbatore.
quoted_passages: I remembered my days at the pump works in Coimbatore and Subramaniam with his steel rod.
I asked a mechanic to press the rod against the housing and listen to the bearing.
